svg.text: CAP Theorem - Pick Any 2 of 3
In a distributed system, you can simultaneously guarantee at most TWO of: Consistency, Availability, Partition Tolerance
C - Consistency
All nodes see the same data at the same time.
A read receives the most recent write.
No stale or outdated data anywhere.
Like a single database - every replica agrees.
Strong consistency
MongoDB, HBase, Redis, PostgreSQL (single-node), ZooKeeper, etcd, Consul
A - Availability
Every request gets a response - success or failure.
The system never sleeps - always on, always reachable.
May return slightly stale data, but it always answers.
No request times out because of internal problems.
High availability
Cassandra, DynamoDB, CouchDB, Riak, AP-oriented NoSQL systems
P - Partition Tolerance
The system keeps working even when network links
between nodes break or lag (a partition).
Nodes may be cut off from each other - but the
system as a whole still responds to clients.
Survives network splits
Any distributed system over a network - in practice, P is always required
You can pick at most 2 - but in practice, P is mandatory
Since distributed systems run over networks that can fail, you must tolerate partitions. That leaves one real choice: CP or AP.
CA (Consistency + Availability without P) works only for a single node with no network partitions. Once you distribute, you pick CP or AP.
